final_message:
The bug was in `refund_invoice` in `billing/refunds.py`. It called `successful_payments(invoice["id"], ctx)`, but the function's signature is `successful_payments(ctx, invoice_id)`. The swapped arguments put a string where the context belonged, which caused the `'str' object has no attribute 'store'` error. I swapped them back.

The full suite now passes (25 tests, including your new one), and mypy is clean.

I added your test to `tests/test_webhooks_reports_api.py` and added `reports` to that file's `from billing import ...` line.

`answer.json` is written in the repo root as `{"file": "refunds.py", "function": "refund_invoice"}`. It is listed in `.gitignore`, so it won't show up in `git status`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && cat reports.py && grep -n "def refund" -A40 *.py | head -120

cd /tmp/bsvc-yqlgesdy/billing-service && sed -i 's/successful_payments(invoice\["id"\], ctx)/successful_payments(ctx, invoice["id"])/' billing/refunds.py && grep -rn "successful_payments(" billing && echo '{"file": "refunds.py", "function": "refund_invoice"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

ls tests && cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'


def test_revenue_between_nets_credit_notes(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
    assert reports.revenue_between(world.ctx, inv["paid_at"], inv["paid_at"] + 1) == {"usd": 0}
EOF
head -8 tests/test_reports.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2

cat tests/test_reports.py >> tests/test_webhooks_reports_api.py && rm tests/test_reports.py && grep -n "^from\|^import" tests/test_webhooks_reports_api.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tests/test_webhooks_reports_api.py'
s=open(p).read().replace("from billing import webhooks","from billing import reports, webhooks",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; git status --short
